alex: deploybot fired for elevated canary p95 in nightshift deploy (v4.1.2, us-west). p95 1.05s, threshold 350ms. canary = 12%. auto-revert blocked by release-window. thoughts?
priya: ouch. blast radius? any reserved customers on that slice?
toby: only internal testing customers. low blast. i'd prefer pin+rollback for canary to be safe.
deploybot: [ALERT] canary_p95_threshold (id cb-9009). metrics: p95=1050ms, errors=normal. auto-revert suppressed per policy.
sre-bot: recommend: 1) pin canary route to v4.1.1, 2) run rollback for canary slice, 3) drop batch-size to 1 if we need temporary mitigation.
priya: pin first to stop more users hitting it. i'll pin now: `redwood route pin --route=canary --version=v4.1.1 --who=priya`
deploybot: [ACTION] Route pinned by priya at 4920012352. pinned -> v4.1.1.
toby: executing rollback for canary now: `./rollback-script --target=v4.1.1 --region=us-west --slice=canary` starting 03:19 UTC
deploybot: [ACTION] Rollback started by toby at 4920012360. progress: 30% -> 70% -> 100%.
toby: rollback done. p95 back to ~310ms. monitoring for 10m.
alex: nice. priya, can you update release-notes and tag the commit "rollback-nightshift-4920012345"? also open postmortem ticket ROLLBACK-789 assigned to eng-ml to look at kv-cache thrash.
priya: release notes updated: "Canary rolled back to v4.1.1 due to increased latency; investigating kv-cache eviction interaction." commit tagged.
marta-cs: i'll prep a short note for impacted devs and post to #customer-ops. send me exact timestamps.
sre-bot: monitoring: 10m p95 stable, error rate unchanged. closing incident if stable for 15m.
alex: thanks everyone. follow-up: eng-ml to run reproducer against kvcache TTL and kernel selection. closing thread for now.
